title: Sam Altman Told the White House He Supports Slowing AI Development. Here's Why That Matters for AI Stocks.
excerpt: AI investing might be shifting from a race for speed to a race for scale and regulatory readiness, giving the biggest players an even stronger edge.
content_html:
In late July, Sam Altman went to Washington, D.C., to brief lawmakers on OpenAI's next-frontier model after one of its systems autonomously hacked another artificial intelligence (AI) platform, Hugging Face, and then pivoted to attack a customer's cloud account. Coming out of those meetings, he told reporters he supports slowing the pace of AI development, said he had seen the draft framework for implementing President Donald Trump's AI executive order, and confirmed he would meet with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to discuss how to vet newer AI models before release.

That is a long way from the early days of move-fast-and-ship models, and it reflects a real shift in how OpenAI thinks about risk.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

For AI-focused companies, this points to a future where model releases are less about racing the calendar and more about clearing regulatory and safety hurdles. The White House framework calls on firms to submit advanced models to the government for testing before launch, and bills like the AI Kill Switch Act would give regulators the power to order a slowdown or shutdown if a system crosses certain lines. That means AI stocks are no longer just about who has the best technology. They are also about who can invest in governance, security, and compliance without choking off their own innovation.

What does this mean for AI investors?

Paradoxically, that kind of environment often favors the largest players. If you own names like Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), or Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), heavier vetting and stricter safeguards might actually deepen their moats. They already spend billions on security, auditing, and infrastructure, and can absorb the costs of slower deployment and more testing. Smaller pure-play AI start-ups, on the other hand, may find that the bar for releasing a frontier model is suddenly beyond their reach, especially if regulators start expecting third-party red-teaming and formal safety reviews.

Altman's comments also matter for stock valuation. When the person running one of the most important AI labs says the industry should slow down, it means investors should rethink the more aggressive growth assumptions baked into some AI stocks. The story is shifting from infinite models at infinite speed to earn the right to innovate by proving you can control what you build. If you are holding or considering AI names, it is worth asking not just how fast they can ship the next model, but how prepared they are for a world where regulators and even the industry's own leaders are asking them to tap the brakes.

content_html_zh:
7 月底，山姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 前往华盛顿特区，向立法者介绍 OpenAI 的下一个前沿模型，此前 OpenAI 的一个系统自主攻击了另一个人工智能 (AI) 平台 Hugging Face，然后转向攻击客户的云帐户。 在这些会议结束后，他告诉记者，他支持放慢人工智能的发展步伐，并表示他已经看到了执行唐纳德·特朗普总统人工智能行政命令的框架草案，并确认他将与白宫办公厅主任苏西·威尔斯会面，讨论如何在发布之前审查新的人工智能模型。

这与早期的“快速行动并交付”模型相去甚远，它反映了 OpenAI 对风险的看法发生了真正的转变。

错过了 2009 年的 Nvidia？ 这个罕见的信号再次闪烁。 2009年，一家名不见经传的芯片制造商英伟达发出了“双倍下跌”的信号。 多年来，对于一家规模仅为 Nvidia 1/100 的公司来说，同样的“完全确信”信号闪烁。 继续 ”

对于专注于人工智能的公司来说，这预示着未来模型的发布不再是为了赶时间，而是更多地为了清除监管和安全障碍。 白宫框架呼吁企业在发布前向政府提交先进模型进行测试，而《人工智能终止开关法案》等法案将赋予监管机构在系统超过某些界限时下令减速或关闭的权力。 这意味着人工智能股票不再仅仅取决于谁拥有最好的技术。 它们还涉及谁可以在不阻碍自身创新的情况下投资治理、安全和合规性。

这对人工智能投资者意味着什么？

矛盾的是，这种环境往往有利于最大的参与者。 如果你拥有像微软（纳斯达克股票代码：MSFT）、Alphabet（纳斯达克股票代码：GOOG）（纳斯达克股票代码：GOOGL）或英伟达（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）这样的名字，更严格的审查和更严格的保护措施实际上可能会加深他们的护城河。 他们已经在安全、审计和基础设施上花费了数十亿美元，并且可以吸收较慢的部署和更多测试的成本。 另一方面，规模较小的纯人工智能初创企业可能会发现发布前沿模型的门槛突然超出了他们的能力范围，特别是如果监管机构开始期待第三方红​​队和正式的安全审查。

奥特曼的评论对于股票估值也很重要。 当最重要的人工智能实验室之一的负责人表示该行业应该放缓时，这意味着投资者应该重新考虑一些人工智能股票中更激进的增长假设。 故事正在以无限的速度从无限的模型转变为通过证明你可以控制你所构建的东西来赢得创新的权利。 如果你持有或考虑人工智能公司，那么值得问的不仅是他们能够以多快的速度推出下一个模型，而且还应该问他们为监管机构甚至行业领导者要求他们踩刹车的世界做好了多少准备。
